plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 9: Systems of Equations and Inequalities
plan.contextChunk: This figure is one graph on a dotted coordinate grid showing two straight lines and the point at which they cross. The horizontal axis is labeled x and carries integer ticks from -6 to 6; the vertical axis is labeled y with integer ticks from -5 to 5, and each axis ends in arrowheads. A blue line of negative slope enters at the upper left and descends to the lower right, meeting the vertical axis just below the origin; a blue label at the left edge reads x + 2y = -1. A red line of positive slope climbs from the lower left to the upper right and meets the vertical axis at 3; a red label at the lower left reads -x + y = 3. Both lines end in arrowheads at each extremity. A filled black dot marks the single crossing, in the second quadrant just left of the vertical axis and slightly above the horizontal axis, and the coordinates printed above it read (-7/3, 2/3) with the fractions stacked. Drawing both equations against shared axes converts the algebraic system into a picture whose solution is a location. The graph makes visible that these lines meet at exactly one point, so the system has a single solution.

interactionPlan.concept: Graphing two linear equations on shared axes turns an algebraic system into a picture: the single point where the lines cross is the ordered pair that satisfies both equations at once.
elements: Dotted square coordinate grid spanning x from -6 to 6 and y from -5 to 5, one unit per cell
Horizontal x-axis, black, with arrowheads at both ends and integer tick labels -6 through 6
Vertical y-axis, black, with arrowheads at both ends and integer tick labels -5 through 5
Axis names: italic 'x' at the right end of the horizontal axis, italic 'y' at the top of the vertical axis
Blue line of negative slope (slope -1/2) crossing the y-axis just below the origin at -1/2, entering upper-left and exiting lower-right, arrowheads at both ends
Blue equation label at the far left of the blue line reading 'x + 2y = -1'
Red line of positive slope (slope 1) crossing the y-axis at 3, rising from lower-left to upper-right, arrowheads at both ends
Red equation label at the lower left reading '-x + y = 3'
Filled black dot at the intersection in the second quadrant, just left of the y-axis and slightly above the x-axis
Stacked-fraction coordinate annotation above the dot reading (-7/3, 2/3)
Dashed black guide segments (appear on click) dropping from the intersection dot to the x-axis and across to the y-axis
Substitution check panel (appears on click) showing each equation with the dot's coordinates substituted and both sides evaluated
Status caption reporting 'one solution' / 'no solution — parallel lines' / 'solution off-grid'

interactions.label: Blue line constant c in x + 2y = c
interactions.teaches: Shifting one line up or down slides the crossing point along the other line — the solution is a location determined jointly by both equations, not by either alone.

interactions.label: Red line slope m in y = m·x + 3
interactions.teaches: Rotating a line about its y-intercept moves the crossing point, and when its slope matches the blue line's -1/2 the lines are parallel and the system has no solution.
Selecting the intersection dot substitutes its coordinates into both equations at once, showing the same ordered pair makes both statements true.

demo_steps.title: The original system
demo_steps.narration: Two lines are drawn on one grid: blue x + 2y = -1 falling to the right, red -x + y = 3 rising to the right. They cross exactly once, in the second quadrant.

demo_steps.title: Read the solution
demo_steps.narration: Click the black dot: dashed guides drop to the axes at x = -7/3 and y = 2/3, and both equations check out when those values are substituted.

demo_steps.title: Slide the blue line
demo_steps.narration: Change the constant to c = 3 and the blue line shifts up; the crossing point slides along the red line to a new place, but there is still exactly one solution.

demo_steps.title: Rotate the red line
demo_steps.narration: Flatten the red line's slope toward -0.5 and watch the intersection race away to the left, off the visible grid — the solution still exists but is far from the origin.

demo_steps.title: Parallel: no solution
demo_steps.narration: At slope exactly -0.5 the red line is parallel to the blue line. The lines never meet, so the system has no solution at all.

demo_steps.title: Back to one crossing
demo_steps.narration: Tilt the red line back to a positive slope and a single crossing reappears — orientation, not position, decides whether a solution exists.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A solution to a system is not a number but a point: the one ordered pair that lies on both lines simultaneously — and if the lines are parallel, no such point exists.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Square-aspect Cartesian plane on a light dotted grid, x from -6 to 6 and y from -5 to 5, black axes with arrowheads and italic x / y axis names. Blue (#1a6b8f-ish teal-blue) line with slope -1/2 through y-intercept -1/2, labeled 'x + 2y = -1' in matching blue at the left edge near where the line leaves the grid. Red line with slope 1 through y-intercept 3, labeled '-x + y = 3' in red at the lower left. Both lines drawn with arrowheads at both visible ends. A solid black dot marks the intersection just left of the y-axis, slightly above the x-axis, with a stacked-fraction label (-7/3, 2/3) set above and to the right of it. Equation labels must update live as the sliders change (e.g. 'x + 2y = 3', '-x + y = 3' rewritten as slope-intercept when rotated), and the coordinate label recomputes to exact fractions where possible. When the lines are parallel, hide the dot and show a caption 'No solution — parallel lines'; when the intersection leaves the grid, keep the caption 'Solution off-grid' with an arrow at the grid edge pointing toward it. Click state adds dashed grey drop-lines to both axes and a small substitution panel below the plot echoing each equation with values plugged in and both sides evaluated in the line's own color.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for the blue line's y-intercept: the learner shifts x + 2y = c up or down, the intersection point with the red line moves or exits the grid, and a system's solution is seen as the point satisfying both equations.
- Slider for the red line's slope: the learner rotates -x + y = 3 about its y-intercept, the crossing location updates and can become parallel to the blue line, clarifying how line orientation controls whether there is one or no visible solution.

authoredContext:
We gain an important perspective on systems of equations by looking at the graphical representation. See the figure to find that the equations intersect at the solution. We do not need to ask whether there may be a second solution because observing the graph confirms that the system has exactly one solution.

This graph displays a system of two linear equations plotted on a coordinate plane. The blue line represents the equation x + 2y = -1, while the red line represents the equation -x + y = 3. The point where these two lines intersect, indicated by a black dot, is the solution to the system of equations and is labeled as (-7/3, 2/3). The x-axis ranges from -6 to 6, and the y-axis ranges from -5 to 5, with a grid background to aid in reading the coordinates.

discrepancies: The intersection coordinate label (−7/3, 2/3) is placed to the right of the dot, straddling the y-axis; its white background box hides the y-axis tick label '3' and overlaps the axis line. In the source the label sits clear of the axis, to the upper-left of the dot.

The x- and y-axes render as broken/dashed dark segments rather than the solid black arrowed axes of the source, weakening the axis/grid distinction (the source has solid black axes over a faint dotted grid).
The dotted grid is much fainter and thinner than the source's clearly visible dotted grid, so the coordinate mesh reads as nearly blank at inline size.
Extra on-figure/panel status text ('One solution: (-7/3, 2/3)') and the hint copy add chrome not present in the source figure (minor, panel-side).
Equation labels ('x + 2y = −1', '−x + y = 3') are smaller relative to the plot than in the source, where they are prominent primary annotations.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful recreation of the two-line system with correct solution point, colors, arrowed lines and equation labels, backed by genuinely useful sliders, a check-the-solution action and a 6-step guided demo; the main weaknesses are the coordinate label colliding with the y-axis and hiding the '3' tick, and axes that render dashed with an over-faint grid.

feedback.rationale: Concept, structure, and interactions are correct; the remaining issues are implementation details (label collision with the y-axis tick, dashed axes, over-faint grid, label sizing) that call for rendering fixes rather than a new plan.

discrepancies: The intersection coordinate label (−7/3, 2/3) sits further left and lower than in the source (source places it up-right of the dot near the y-axis at ~y=3); the comma between the two fractions is barely visible at inline size, so the pair reads as two loose fractions.

Equation labels are placed slightly differently: the blue 'x + 2y = −1' is pulled inside the grid rather than hanging off the left margin as in the source, and both are rendered in a lighter/smaller italic than the source's prominent colored labels.
Gridline dotting is slightly denser/darker than the source's faint dotted graph paper, giving the background a bit more visual weight.
The UI status readout writes the solution with an ASCII hyphen ('(-7/3, 2/3)') instead of a true minus sign, inconsistent with the typography used on the canvas.
evaluation.notes: A very close reproduction of the source graph (correct dotted grid, axis ranges, double-arrow axes and lines, correct blue/red equations and the (−7/3, 2/3) crossing), backed by genuinely useful sliders, a check-the-solution toggle and a 6-step demo that correctly exposes one-solution / parallel-no-solution cases; the only real weaknesses are the coordinate label's placement and its cramped comma/fraction typography.
action_items: Move the (−7/3, 2/3) label up-right of the dot as in the source and widen the comma spacing (or add a small gap token) so the ordered pair reads unambiguously.
Increase the size/weight of the two colored equation labels slightly and anchor them just outside the grid's left edge to match the source's prominence.
Use the Unicode minus (−) consistently in the UI status text and popup bodies to match the canvas typography.
Lighten the dotted gridline stroke (smaller dash, lower opacity) to better match the faint graph-paper look of the source.

feedback.rationale: Concept and interaction plan are correct (all 5s, no failure modes); remaining issues are purely cosmetic implementation details like label placement, typography, and gridline styling.
